title: 15 Commission Based Jobs in India 2026: Real Roles and Rates
summary: Loan agent, insurance, real estate and sales roles, reported rates, how payouts work, and how to avoid MLM traps.
body_markdown:
Commission based jobs pay you for each sale or result, not for hours worked. Common roles in India include selling financial products with GroMo, loan agent, credit card agent, insurance advisor, real estate agent and mutual fund distributor. Income is uncapped but never guaranteed, and it's often uneven in the first few months. If you're comparing apps rather than roles, see our list of[commission earning apps](https://gromo.in/blog/commission-earning-app/) .


Below are 15 commission jobs with reported rates where a source gives them, the skills needed and the steps to start. Rates change by company and product, so confirm them before you begin.


# Job Starting cost Skills needed Best for


1 Selling Financial Products With GroMo None Basic phone use; free training in the app Anyone 18 or older


2 Loan Agent (DSA) Very low Loan basics, local network People with business contacts


3 Credit Card Agent None Card knowledge People with salaried contacts


4 Insurance Advisor Low IRDAI-required training People with wide networks


5 Real Estate Agent Low Local market knowledge People in growing property markets


6 Mutual Fund Distributor Low NISM V-A, AMFI ARN People good at explaining money


7 Direct Sales Executive None Persuasion, walking the market People who enjoy field work


8 Telesales Executive None Clear calling Freshers who like talking


9 Affiliate Marketer None Content, audience People with a blog or social following


10 Car or Bike Sales Executive None Product knowledge, communication People who enjoy vehicles


11 Edtech Sales Counsellor None Counselling, patience Good communicators


12 Recruitment Consultant None LinkedIn, screening People with HR or industry contacts


13 Merchant Onboarding Agent None Local market contacts People who know shopkeepers


14 Advertising Sales Agent None Business contacts, negotiation People who know local businesses


15 Campus Ambassador None College network College students


Starting-cost labels are our own rough estimates: None, Very low, Low, Medium and High. Actual costs depend on your city and setup.


How this list is ranked: GroMo comes first because it's free to join and has no targets. The rest follow the roles that appear most often in top-ranking Indian guides and job portals, from those open to beginners to those needing licences or experience.


## 1. Selling Financial Products With GroMo: Bank-paid commissions, no stock


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Basic phone use; free training in the app | **Best for:** Anyone 18 or older


Selling financial products with GroMo tops this list because it costs nothing to start and needs only a smartphone. GroMo is a free app where you help people apply for credit cards, savings accounts, loans and demat accounts from partner banks, and you earn a commission when the application is approved. On GroMo, credit cards pay up to ₹2,000, savings accounts up to ₹1,000, demat accounts up to ₹450, and personal loans up to 4.5% of the loan amount (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). Unlike most commission jobs, there's no joining fee, boss or monthly target, and you can start with people you already know. The pay is commission only, with no fixed salary, and only approved applications earn; you must be 18 or older.


How to start:


1. Download the GroMo app and register free with your phone number.
2. Finish the one-time verification and the free in-app training.
3. Share a product link with someone who genuinely needs it, then track the application in the app.


## 2. Loan Agent (DSA): Paid per disbursed loan


**Starting cost:** Very low | **Skills:** Loan basics, local network | **Best for:** People with business contacts


Loan agents earn when a bank or NBFC disburses a loan they sourced. One 2026 guide reports 1% to 2.5% on personal loans, with rates negotiated by volume (MyMudra, retrieved 2026-11-06). Read[what a loan agent does](https://gromo.in/blog/what-is-a-loan-agent/) for a full picture of the role.


How to start:


1. Learn eligibility rules for common loans.
2. Join through a lender or platform.
3. Never charge a borrower for approval.


## 3. Credit Card Agent: Paid per approved card


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Card knowledge | **Best for:** People with salaried contacts


Credit card agents earn per approved card. One 2026 guide reports ₹500 to ₹3,000 a card (MyMudra, retrieved 2026-11-06). Commission depends on the bank and on the customer's approval, so check eligibility before sharing a link.


How to start:


1. Learn the main card types.
2. Join through a bank partner or an app.
3. Check the customer's eligibility first.


## 4. Insurance Advisor: Paid on premiums and renewals


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** IRDAI-required training | **Best for:** People with wide networks


Insurance advisors earn on the premiums of policies they sell. One guide reports 10% to 25% on new policies and 5% to 10% on renewals (Niva Bupa, retrieved 2026-11-06). Renewals can build steady income, but you must join through a licensed insurer or broker.


How to start:


1. Choose a licensed insurer or broker.
2. Complete the required training.
3. Explain exclusions honestly.


## 5. Real Estate Agent: Paid brokerage per deal


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Local market knowledge | **Best for:** People in growing property markets


Real estate agents earn brokerage on sales and rentals. Deals are big but infrequent, so months can pass without income. Check your state's RERA rules on agent registration before you take on property sales.


How to start:


1. Learn your local market.
2. Check the state RERA agent rules.
3. Start with rentals to build experience.


## 6. Mutual Fund Distributor: Trail commission on investments


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** NISM V-A, AMFI ARN | **Best for:** People good at explaining money


Mutual fund distributors earn trail commission while clients stay invested, which builds income slowly but steadily. You must pass NISM Series V-A and hold an AMFI ARN before selling, and you can't promise returns. For a broader view, see[finance business ideas](https://gromo.in/blog/finance-business-ideas/) .


How to start:


1. Pass NISM Series V-A.
2. Get your ARN from AMFI.
3. Start with SIPs for people you know.


## 7. Direct Sales Executive: Field sales with incentives


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Persuasion, walking the market | **Best for:** People who enjoy field work


Direct sales executives sell products to homes and shops, often with a small fixed salary plus incentives. Check whether you must buy stock yourself; a real job doesn't require that, and it's a warning sign of a pyramid scheme.


How to start:


1. Check the company and offer letter.
2. Ask about fixed pay and incentives.
3. Refuse to buy stock to get the job.


## 8. Telesales Executive: Incentives on phone sales


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Clear calling | **Best for:** Freshers who like talking


Telesales roles usually pay a fixed amount plus commission, and one listing we saw paid 10% to 15% commission on sales beyond a target (job listing, retrieved 2026-11-06). Our guide to[work from home sales jobs](https://gromo.in/blog/work-from-home-sales-jobs/) has more pay examples.


How to start:


1. Ask for fixed pay and target in writing.
2. Check whether fixed pay depends on target.
3. Keep a quiet calling space.


## 9. Affiliate Marketer: Commission per online sale


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Content, audience | **Best for:** People with a blog or social following


Affiliate marketers earn a commission when someone buys through their link. Most programmes are free to join, but income depends on an audience that trusts you, so it usually takes months to build.


How to start:


1. Pick a product area you know.
2. Join one affiliate programme.
3. Disclose your links in every post.


## 10. Car or Bike Sales Executive: Salary plus sale incentives


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Product knowledge, communication | **Best for:** People who enjoy vehicles


Vehicle sales executives at dealerships usually earn a base salary plus an incentive per vehicle sold. Festive months can bring strong earnings, but targets are tight, so ask existing staff what they really make.


How to start:


1. Apply at local dealerships.
2. Learn the models and finance options.
3. Ask about incentive slabs before joining.


## 11. Edtech Sales Counsellor: Incentive per enrolment


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Counselling, patience | **Best for:** Good communicators


Edtech counsellors earn incentives for each course enrolment. Pressure can be high, so ask about targets upfront, and never push a family into a course loan they don't understand.


How to start:


1. Ask about targets and lead supply.
2. Learn the course and refund policy.
3. Be honest about fees and loans.


## 12. Recruitment Consultant: Paid per successful hire


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** LinkedIn, screening | **Best for:** People with HR or industry contacts


Recruitment consultants earn a fee when a candidate they refer gets hired and stays for the agreed time. You can work with an agency or independently, and reliable candidates get you repeat clients.


How to start:


1. Pick one industry to focus on.
2. Join an agency or find a first client.
3. Agree the fee and replacement terms in writing.


## 13. Merchant Onboarding Agent: Paid per signed-up shop


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Local market contacts | **Best for:** People who know shopkeepers


Merchant agents sign up shops for QR codes and card machines on behalf of fintech firms. Pay is often per successful activation, so confirm what counts as success, and explain any charges clearly to shopkeepers.


How to start:


1. Find a partner role with a known company.
2. Learn the product and charges.
3. Confirm what counts as a paid activation.


## 14. Advertising Sales Agent: Commission on ad deals


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Business contacts, negotiation | **Best for:** People who know local businesses


Advertising sales agents sell ad space for local newspapers, cable networks, websites and hoardings. Commission is paid per deal, and your local business contacts are your main asset, so it suits people with long ties to one town.


How to start:


1. Pick one local media partner.
2. Agree commission and payment dates in writing.
3. Start with businesses you know.


## 15. Campus Ambassador: Incentives for student referrals


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** College network | **Best for:** College students


Campus ambassadors promote brands and courses at their colleges in return for incentives or rewards. It's a light way to practise sales, but check that rewards are paid in cash rather than just certificates. GroMo needs you to be 18 or older.


How to start:


1. Apply to a known company's programme.
2. Check how rewards are paid.
3. Don't pressure friends to buy.


## How Much Does GroMo Pay for Each Product?


Product on GroMo Pays partners up to


SBI Credit Card ₹2,000 per approved card


HDFC Secured Credit Card ₹1,750 per approved card


Axis Saving Account ₹1,000 per account


Digi Credit Personal Loan 4.5% of the loan amount


Kotak 811 Super Account ₹600 per account


Kotak Securities Demat Account ₹450 per account


The SBI Credit Card pays partners up to ₹2,000 per approved card (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). Commission is paid only on approval.


The Axis Saving Account pays up to ₹1,000 per successful account (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). Many other products pay less.


The Digi Credit Personal Loan pays up to 4.5% of the loan amount, and most other lenders pay less (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). Check the live payout in the app.


## How much can you earn from commission based jobs?


Commission income has no fixed number. One job portal reports that new commission-based professionals earn ₹15,000 to ₹30,000 a month and experienced advisors earn more (TrueJobs, retrieved 2026-11-06), but those are indicative figures and many beginners earn less. The first few months are usually the slowest, so keep other income or savings while you build up.


## Commission only or salary plus commission: which is better?


Salary plus commission is better if you need regular income, and commission only is better if you want flexibility and have some financial cushion. Commission-only work has no shifts or boss, but there's no pay without results. Our guide to the[credit card sales job](https://gromo.in/blog/credit-card-sales-job/) compares both using one role.


## How do you spot an MLM or fake commission job?


A fake commission job makes you pay to join, buy stock, or earn mainly by recruiting other people. A genuine commission role pays you for real sales to real customers. Ask who pays you and for what, and check the company's registration. If the pitch is about building a downline, walk away.


## How do you succeed in a commission based job?


Success in a commission job comes from steady follow-up and honest selling. Talk to more people, recommend only what fits, and track every lead. Trust brings repeat customers and referrals, which are the cheapest sales you'll ever get. Our guide on[how to convince a customer](https://gromo.in/blog/how-to-convince-customer/) gives simple scripts.


**GroMo** is a free app where partners help customers apply for credit cards, loans, savings accounts and demat accounts from partner banks, and earn a commission on approval.


## FAQ: Commission Based Jobs


### What are commission based jobs?


They pay you for each sale or result instead of a fixed salary. Examples include loan agent, insurance advisor, real estate agent and selling financial products with GroMo.


### Which commission job pays the most in India?


There's no single highest payer. Real estate and insurance can pay well per deal, but income is uneven. Your network, product and consistency matter more than the job title.


### Are commission based jobs real?


Many are, but scams exist too. Avoid any job that charges a joining fee, makes you buy stock, or pays mainly for recruiting others.


### Can freshers do commission based jobs?


Yes. Telesales, credit card agent roles and selling financial products with GroMo are open to beginners. Expect slower income at the start.


### Is commission income taxable in India?


Yes. Commission is taxable income, and TDS may be deducted. Show it in your income tax return, and ask a CA if you're unsure.


### Can I do a commission job from home?


Yes. Selling financial products, telesales, affiliate marketing and recruitment can all be done from home with a phone or laptop.


GroMo (Vitrak Technologies Pvt Ltd) is a distribution platform. GroMo isn't a bank, NBFC, insurer or investment adviser. All products are offered by their respective RBI, IRDAI or SEBI-regulated providers.


Partner earnings depend on effort, product mix and customer eligibility. Any figures shown are illustrative. They aren't typical and aren't promised.


Sources: Top-ranking guides checked: TrueJobs, MyMudra, Niva Bupa, Ruloans and AmbitionBox, retrieved 2026-11-06. GroMo product catalogue, commission rates by product, retrieved 2026-11-06.


## Disclaimer


GroMo doesn't promise any level of income. Commissions are set by partner banks, vary by product and campaign, and are paid only on approved applications; check the live commission in the GroMo app. Starting-cost labels are our own rough estimates, and any pay figures from other sites or job listings are what those sources state, not a guarantee. GroMo is available only to users aged 18 and above. Everything above is general information, not financial, legal or career advice.
